## Highlights

- **Task and automation agents on a provider subscription start again.** From v0.5.80 to v0.5.83, every managed agent turn served by a **Subscription key** or **Subscription broker** credential, in a task or in an automation's `agent` step, failed before its agent started, with `reserveTurnBudget answered with an unexpected shape — the turn cannot be sized`. Such a turn now runs as one request at no cost: request and token limits bind it, cost limits do not. Turns on an **API key** or **Environment variable** credential are admitted as before. See [Use subscriptions in tasks, not in chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/providers#use-subscriptions-in-tasks-not-in-chat). [#4793](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4793)

## Upgrade notes

- Deploy the Tale platform and the Tale CLI together. The backend applies two forward-only database migrations at boot, `0198_automation_version_lineage.sql` and `0199_automation_deployment_events.sql`; both are safe while the previous image still runs during a rolling deploy. The API contract stays at `3.35.0`.
- `0198_automation_version_lineage.sql` adds three nullable columns to `app.automations`, `based_on_version`, `restored_from_version` and `change_summary`: the version a saved version started from, the version a restore brought back, and what the version changed, as counts and flags only. Versions the new image saves fill them in; versions saved before the upgrade, or by the previous image during the roll, leave them empty, which Tale treats as not recorded.
- `0199_automation_deployment_events.sql` creates `app.automation_deployment_events`, which records each time a version of an automation went live and keeps it as long as the automation exists. It fills the table from existing data: every `automation.deployed` entry the audit log still holds for an automation that still exists, then, for each automation whose live version those entries do not show, one entry that records that version as live, with who last deployed it and when. An automation's deployment history therefore starts with the oldest deploy your audit log still holds. A deploy the previous image makes during the roll writes no entry; the new image's next deploy of that automation records the version it finds live first. See [Versions and deployments](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/editor#versions).
